encounter.reason: Routine Diabetic Follow-up and neuropathy review

documents.title: Endocrinology Outpatient Progress Note
documents.content: Patient Eleanor Vance (60 yo F) presents for diabetes management. Reports bilateral foot numbness and burning tingling in lower extremities consistent with diabetic peripheral neuropathy. Current medications: Metformin 1000mg BID, Glipizide 5mg daily. Fundoscopic exam reveals mild non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy. Advised tight glycemic control.

diagnostics.conclusion: HbA1c severely elevated at 10.4% (Ref: <5.7%). Indicative of uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with chronic microvascular risk.

encounter.reason: Substernal chest pain radiating to left jaw and diaphoresis

documents.title: Emergency Department Admission Note
documents.content: 45-year-old male arrived via EMS with acute severe crushing substernal chest pressure, diaphoresis, and shortness of breath starting 2 hours prior. ECG demonstrates ST-segment elevations in leads V1-V4 consistent with acute anterior STEMI. Emergent cardiac catheterization initiated.

diagnostics.conclusion: Troponin I critically elevated at 14.80 ng/mL (Ref: <0.04 ng/mL). Consistent with Acute Myocardial Infarction.

encounter.reason: Persistent productive cough, fever, and right pleuritic chest pain

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation Note
documents.content: 31 yo female with 1-week history of worsening dyspnea, chills, and purulent sputum. Oxygen saturation 92% on ambient air. Right lower lung base reveals crackles and bronchial breath sounds. Started on empiric Levofloxacin for community-acquired pneumonia.

diagnostics.conclusion: Frontal and lateral chest radiographs demonstrate dense consolidation in the right lower lobe with prominent air bronchograms, typical for bacterial lobar pneumonia. No pleural effusion.

documents.title: Hospital Inpatient Discharge Summary
documents.content: 68-year-old male with ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 30%) admitted with 15-lb fluid weight gain, severe orthopnea, and bilateral 3+ pitting edema. Responded briskly to IV Furosemide diuresis with 6L net negative fluid balance. Discharge weight stabilized.

diagnostics.conclusion: BNP significantly elevated at 1,890 pg/mL (Ref: <100 pg/mL), confirming acute decompensated heart failure.

encounter.reason: Lupus nephritis surveillance and proteinuria check

documents.title: Nephrology Clinic Note
documents.content: 35 yo female with known Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) and Class IV Lupus Nephritis. Currently maintained on Mycophenolate Mofetil and Hydroxychloroquine. Evaluated for increased peripheral edema and elevated blood pressure.

diagnostics.conclusion: Urine protein to creatinine ratio markedly elevated at 3.2 mg/mg (Ref: <0.2 mg/mg), demonstrating active nephrotic-range proteinuria and lupus flare.
